narration: Sunday. The first of November, 2015. Ten thirty-three in the morning.

notes: Reported wording only, reset in house type; do not imitate the Weibo interface
narration: In the city of Ningbo, the highway police post a short notice online. Sudden traffic control.
The entrances to the Hangzhou Bay Bridge are closed.

motion: pull back; distance counter runs along the bridge
narration: The bridge is thirty-five kilometres long. It crosses open sea.

cue: And on the road towards it
narration: And on the road towards it, there is one car that does not know.
The man inside left his grandmother's hundredth birthday party a few minutes ago. He left in a hurry. He is wearing a white coat.
He controls more money than any hedge fund manager in China. This year, the market lost five trillion dollars.

motion: one green line climbs through the red
notes: Reported figure (NYT); shape is illustrative, label it so
narration: His best fund is up three hundred and fifty-seven percent.
For twenty-two years, he has known everything first.

motion: cut to black on the line
narration: Not today.

on_screen: THE MAN WHO ALWAYS KNEW FIRST

motion: push towards the back of the room; scoreboard appears
narration: His name is Xu Xiang. You have probably never heard it.

on_screen: 私募一哥 HEDGE FUND BROTHER No. 1
narration: In China, they called him Hedge Fund Brother Number One.
He gave almost no interviews.

cue: He came to work in a tracksuit.
narration: He came to work in a tracksuit. He sat at the back of his own trading floor.

motion: rack focus between phones; labels on screens
narration: In meetings he watched two phones. One for prices. One for news.
He let everyone else talk.

cue: A friend put it like this.
on_screen: "Xu Xiang is always trading..." — a longtime friend, to the New York Times Magazine
narration: A friend put it like this. "Xu Xiang is always trading. If he's not trading, he's thinking about trading."

motion: two bars grow; one leaves the frame
narration: His first fund went up three thousand two hundred and seventy percent in five and a half years. Over the same years, the Shanghai index rose eleven.
Nobody could explain it. Plenty of people had a theory.
And in the summer of 2015, somebody decided to find out.

motion: rewind effect; scoreboard spins back to 1990 / ¥0
narration: Go back to 1990.
Shanghai opens a stock exchange. A whole country starts learning what a share is, all at the same time.

cue: Xu Xiang is in his first year
motion: map draws the coast, pin on Ningbo
narration: Xu Xiang is in his first year of high school, in Ningbo, a port city down the coast.

cue: His father works in a factory.
narration: His father works in a factory. His mother keeps the house. Nobody in the family has ever owned a share.
He starts trading anyway, while he is still at school.
There is no teacher. He reads books.
He sits in on lectures. He copies whatever he can find about how foreigners do it.

cue: Then comes the university entrance exam.
narration: Then comes the university entrance exam. In China, that exam decides your life.

motion: push in on the empty desk
narration: He doesn't take it.
Instead, he asks his parents for thirty thousand yuan. About five thousand dollars.
And he carries it to a trading hall on South Liberation Road.

notes: Exact wording of the 'born in 1993' line still to check
narration: Years later, he would say that 1993 was the year he was born.

cue: The hall belongs to Galaxy Securities.
narration: The hall belongs to Galaxy Securities. Second floor, up a concrete staircase.

cue: The prices are written on blackboards
narration: The prices are written on blackboards, in chalk.
The rules change so often that nobody is sure what they are this month.

cue: And he has picked a terrible moment.
motion: chalk-style line climbs then drops off the board
narration: And he has picked a terrible moment. In 1992, the Shanghai index rose a hundred and sixty-seven percent. Between April 1993 and the summer of 1994, it falls by three quarters.

cue: Most of the people in that hall
narration: Most of the people in that hall are finished. In China there is a word for them.
Chives. You cut them. They grow back. You cut them again.

cue: Xu Xiang does not get cut.
narration: Xu Xiang does not get cut.

on_screen: BUY FAST. SELL FAST. ALWAYS GO BIG.
motion: three words land one at a time
narration: He builds a style, and he never changes it. Buy fast. Sell fast. Always go big.

notes: Legend: must keep the RUMOUR tag
narration: By 1995 he is nineteen, and people in Ningbo are telling a story about him. Two Shanghai gangsters, they say, fell out over which of them would get him as a personal trader.

cue: A triad boss had to settle it.
narration: A triad boss had to settle it.

cue: Nobody has ever proved that story.
narration: Nobody has ever proved that story. But people believed it.
At nineteen, he was already someone you could believe that about. Then the market did something that

motion: price line rises into a ceiling and stops
narration: made his whole career possible.
In December 1996, Chinese shares get a ceiling. A stock can rise ten percent in a day. Then it stops. That is the limit.

cue: The rule is there to calm
narration: The rule is there to calm things down. Now think about what it really does.

cue: A stock that hits the ceiling
motion: order book: tall buy stack, empty sell side
narration: A stock that hits the ceiling still has buyers. They wanted in. They couldn't get in. So tomorrow morning, they try again.

cue: The limit does not stop a rush.
motion: queue of small figures forms behind the stack
narration: The limit does not stop a rush. It makes the rush wait in line.

cue: Xu and a handful of traders
narration: Xu and a handful of traders at Galaxy work out how to start that line.
Pick a cheap stock that nobody is watching.

cue: Hit it with one enormous buy order
narration: Hit it with one enormous buy order, out of nowhere.

motion: figures pile in; line hits ceiling
narration: Other traders see the size and pile in. Limit up.
Next morning, the buyers who missed out push it to the limit again.
A few days later, sell everything to the people still arriving.

motion: line drops; the squad is already off frame
narration: Then the price falls. But you are already gone.

cue: The press gives them a name.
on_screen: 涨停板敢死队 LIMIT-UP DEATH SQUAD
notes: Generic newspaper design, no real masthead
narration: The press gives them a name. The Limit-Up Death Squad.

cue: Xu Xiang, in his early twenties
motion: push in on the centre figure
narration: Xu Xiang, in his early twenties, is the captain.

cue: Soon they barely need the trick.
motion: dots light up city by city, lines to Ningbo
narration: Soon they barely need the trick. Traders across the country watch which stocks the Ningbo hall is buying, and buy the same ones.

cue: Their order has become the news.
narration: Their order has become the news.

motion: pan along the cars to the empty space
narration: The others buy sports cars and park them outside the hall.
Xu doesn't. He buys more stock.
There are books about them. Travelling seminars. Copycat squads in other cities.
And in 2003, a newspaper asks the obvious question. Is any of this allowed?
The regulator sends an investigator to Ningbo.

cue: He calls in the big local traders
narration: He calls in the big local traders for what is described as an informal discussion.
The Death Squad vanishes.
For one week.

motion: hard cut back to the full hall
narration: Then the investigator announces that he has found no wrongdoing. And they come back.
Remember that week. It matters later.

motion: scoreboard 2005 / hundreds of millions of yuan
narration: By 2005, the boy with thirty thousand yuan has hundreds of millions.
Ningbo is now too small. He moves to Shanghai, and his timing is perfect.

cue: That same year, a change in the law
narration: That same year, a change in the law lets private funds step out of the shadows and operate in the open. They call them sunshine funds.
In December 2009, he registers his own firm.

on_screen: 泽 Mao ZEdong · 熙 KangXI
notes: Characters and names only; no portraits
narration: He calls it Zexi. Ze, from Mao Zedong. Xi, from Kangxi, the longest-reigning emperor in Chinese history.
Modest, he was not.

motion: counter, then a list of names blacked out line by line
narration: In March 2010 he opens his first fund with one billion yuan. It has fewer than two hundred investors.
Under the rules, that means he never has to say who they are. Remember that, too.
He is at his desk at eight forty-five every morning.

motion: same framing as the morning shot
narration: He is often still there at two the next morning.
His own researchers only find out whether he took their advice at the end of the year, when the results come in.

cue: Friends say he has no hobbies.
narration: Friends say he has no hobbies. There is the market. That is all there is.

cue: The method has grown up with him.
narration: The method has grown up with him. He no longer just hits a stock and runs. He buys a real stake in a small company.

cue: He gets allies onto the board.
narration: He gets allies onto the board.

motion: coins loop back into more shares
narration: The company pays out cash. He uses the cash to buy more, and sells into the rise.
Between 2010 and 2014 he does this with forty-five companies.

motion: two nodes highlight inside the web
narration: His own parents sit as executives and shareholders across the web of firms.
And the results are absurd. One fund returns five hundred and thirty-six percent in four years.
By 2015 he is the hundred and eighty-eighth richest person in China, worth two point two billion dollars.

cue: So who were the two hundred?
motion: the redacted list returns, tag top left
narration: So who were the two hundred? It was said, and never proven, that some of them were the children of very senior officials.

cue: A man who had worked in the industry
narration: A man who had worked in the industry told a reporter that when a powerful client hands you money, it is difficult to say no.

motion: two pins in central Beijing, distance line
narration: In November 2014, Xu opens an office in Beijing. It is less than half a mile from the headquarters of the stock market regulator.
His colleagues later said that was the start of a year spent trying to protect himself. He could feel something coming.
He was right. Then the market did something that

motion: the section 5 ceiling, flipped; line falls into a floor at −10%
narration: made his whole career impossible.

motion: index draws day by day over the edge
narration: Friday, the twelfth of June, 2015. The Chinese market peaks. Then it falls.
In three weeks, a third of its value is gone.

cue: Remember who is in this market.
narration: Remember who is in this market. Two hundred million ordinary people. They make about eighty-five percent of the trades.

cue: Chives, as far as you can see.
narration: Chives, as far as you can see.
The government throws everything at it. Big shareholders are banned from selling. New listings are frozen. State firms are ordered to buy.

cue: They call it the national team
narration: They call it the national team, and it has up to three trillion yuan behind it.
It does not hold.
The twenty-seventh of July. Another plunge.
The twenty-fourth of August. Shanghai falls eight and a half percent, its worst day in eight years.

on_screen: NEW YORK · DOW −1,000 AT THE OPEN
notes: Was a generated scene; every version carried garbled or real exchange logos
narration: In New York, the Dow drops a thousand points at the open. The state newspaper calls it Black Monday.

motion: scoreboard swaps to the market total
narration: Five trillion dollars, gone in ten weeks.
And Zexi?

motion: five green lines rise through the red
narration: In the worst three weeks of the crash, all five of his public funds go up. Every one, by at least twenty percent.

motion: league table, one row climbs to the top
narration: His best fund is up three hundred and fifty-seven percent for the year. First place, out of one thousand six hundred and forty-nine.

cue: His money seemed to step out
narration: His money seemed to step out of the market just before each fall.
In a normal year, that makes you a genius.

cue: In a year when the state itself lost
narration: In a year when the state itself lost, what does it make you?
Meanwhile, in Beijing, people need an answer. The Party's own inspectors have begun going through the stock regulator from top to bottom.
Brokerage executives are being arrested. Everyone in finance is asking the same thing.
Who is next?

notes: Legend: keep the ALLEGATION tag; no real usernames
narration: In September, an anonymous post goes viral. It claims that during the rescue, Zexi worked with a state-owned brokerage to point the government's own buying at a stock Zexi wanted lifted.

on_screen: Zexi denied the claim. No court ruled on it.
narration: Zexi denied it. No court ever ruled on it.

cue: But the regulator is now looking.
narration: But the regulator is now looking. And Xu Xiang is told he may not leave the country.
Nine days later, his grandmother turns one hundred.
The party is small. His grandmother still lives in the neighbourhood where he grew up.
Shortly before ten thirty, according to people who knew him, a warning reaches him. They are coming.
He leaves at once.
He drives north, towards Shanghai. Past the concrete blocks.
Over the river that cuts Ningbo in half.
Out along the bay.

motion: road reduces to one line, one bridge
narration: The fast road to Shanghai has one bridge.

cue: For twenty-two years, his whole edge
narration: For twenty-two years, his whole edge had been knowing before everyone else. This morning he knew, too.
A few minutes late. And not about the bridge.
They stop him there.

notes: Never recreate or show the press photo; we show people reacting to it
narration: That evening, a photograph appears online. White coat. Rimless glasses.

motion: continue the push into their faces
notes: The model would not draw handcuffs; we stay on the reaction
narration: Someone's hand is pulling back his sleeve, and you can see the cuff. He is looking straight into the camera.

cue: The internet does what it does.
motion: comment bubbles stack over the image
narration: The internet does what it does. The coat, people said, looked like a doctor's. Had he been arrested for practising medicine without a licence?
Two hundred million people had just been cut. Now they had someone to look at.
Then, nothing. When reporters reach Zexi's offices in Shanghai and Beijing, the doors are already sealed.

cue: There is a word for what
narration: There is a word for what has happened to him. Shilian. Lost contact.

cue: The firm does not survive it.
narration: The firm does not survive it. As one profile put it: Xu was Zexi.
Thirteen months later, he appears in a courtroom in Qingdao.
And he pleads guilty.
Now we get the answer. How did he always know?

motion: boardroom joins the start of the section 5 diagram
narration: From 2010 to 2015, the court found, Xu worked with executives at thirteen listed companies.

cue: The company would put out good news.
narration: The company would put out good news.
Xu would buy heavily, and the price would climb.
Ordinary investors would see it and rush in.
Then Xu and the executives would sell to them.
He knew first because he had arranged what there was to know.

motion: the two diagrams side by side
narration: Look at it again. It is the same trick as the chalk hall. Start the line. Sell to the people at the back of it.
The only thing that changed in twenty years was the size.
On the twenty-third of January 2017, the sentence. Five and a half years.

motion: figures land one at a time; scoreboard updates
notes: Reported, not published by the court
narration: And a fine reported at eleven billion yuan. One point six billion dollars. The largest ever handed to one person for a financial crime in China.
He does not appeal.
So here is the question this story leaves you with.
In 2003, an investigator looked at the Death Squad and found nothing wrong.
In 2017, a court looked at the grown-up version and sent its captain to prison.
Was he a criminal who finally got caught? Or one player in a game that everybody was playing, picked out because the country needed a face?

on_screen: — a fund manager, to the New York Times Magazine
narration: One fund manager said that many others could have been detained for exactly the same reasons.
The court's answer is simpler. He broke the law. He said so himself.

cue: Both of those can be true.
narration: Both of those can be true.

cue: It cost him more than money.
narration: It cost him more than money. In March 2019, with Xu still in prison, his wife filed for divorce.
They had met in 1998, when he was still the kid from the chalk hall.
Around twenty billion yuan of assets sat frozen.

cue: And the industry he had ruled
narration: And the industry he had ruled banned him from it.

cue: His gift was never picking stocks.
narration: His gift was never picking stocks.
It was knowing first. He built a life on it, and for twenty-two years it worked.

cue: But a man who lives by knowing first
narration: But a man who lives by knowing first has exactly one weakness. The day somebody else knows before he does.

motion: slow pull back; scoreboard: fine reported unpaid
narration: On the ninth of July 2021, Xu Xiang walked out of prison. He was forty-four.

cue: The fine, by the last reports
narration: The fine, by the last reports, had still not been paid.

on_screen: "In China, the losing side doesn't get to sleep at night."
narration: A fund manager in Beijing once summed up the whole business in one sentence. "In China, the losing side doesn't get to sleep at night."

motion: car lights begin to move along the bridge
narration: As for the bridge. It reopened after a little more than half an hour.
The traffic moved on.
